text.subclaim: The Schmidt-rank-at-most-two vector with negative expectation on (I - (1/2) |Ω><Ω|) tensor-powered 4 times, for unnormalized Ω=∑i|ii> in local dimension 3, is conjecturally false.
text.assumptions: Assume the existence of a Schmidt-rank-at-most-two vector with negative expectation on (I - (1/2) |Ω><Ω|) tensor-powered 4 times, for unnormalized Ω=∑i|ii> in local dimension 3.
text.derivation:
The derivation is as follows: 

*   Assume there exists a Schmidt-rank-at-most-two vector with negative expectation on (I - (1/2) |Ω><Ω|) tensor-powered 4 times, for unnormalized Ω=∑i|ii> in local dimension 3.

*   Then, by definition of Schmidt-rank, this vector must have a non-negative expectation value on all positive partial transpose tensors. 

*   However, the tensor (I - (1/2) |Ω><Ω|) has a negative expectation value on any positive partial transpose tensor, since it represents the difference between the identity and a projector onto the subspace of states that are orthogonal to Ω. 

*   Therefore, our assumption is false, and there does not exist a Schmidt-rank-at-most-two vector with negative expectation on (I - (1/2) |Ω><Ω|) tensor-powered 4 times, for unnormalized Ω=∑i|ii> in local dimension 3.
text.falsifier: The falsifier is the existence of any positive partial transpose tensor that has a non-negative expectation value on (I - (1/2) |Ω><Ω|).
text.next_check: An independently executable check would be to compute the expectation values of all positive partial transpose tensors on (I - (1/2) |Ω><Ω|) for an unnormalized Ω=∑i|ii> in local dimension 3 and verify that they are all non-negative. If any such tensor has a negative expectation value, then our conjecture is false.
